scenes.tts: Once an axon is chosen, how does cargo know which branch to go into?
scenes.visual: Title card: Tracks That Point Two Ways. Cargo icons waiting in the cell body at a fork: gold axon, green dendrite.
scenes.narration: Once an axon is chosen, how does cargo know which branch to go into?

scenes.tts: Microtubules link choosing the axon to holding it.
scenes.visual: The stable microtubules in the gold axon from the last chapter, now drawn as tracks.
scenes.narration: Microtubules link choosing the axon to holding it.

scenes.tts: A microtubule has a fast growing plus end and a slower minus end.
scenes.caption: A microtubule has a fast-growing plus end and a slower minus end.
scenes.visual: One microtubule drawn as an arrow: plus at the head, minus at the tail.
scenes.narration: A microtubule has a fast-growing plus end and a slower minus end.

scenes.tts: Motor proteins read that direction. Most kinesins walk toward plus ends. Dynein walks toward minus ends.
scenes.visual: A kinesin walks to the plus end; a dynein walks to the minus end.
scenes.narration: Motor proteins read that direction. Most kinesins walk toward plus ends. Dynein walks toward minus ends.

scenes.tts: Picture a plus end out track. Its plus end points away from the cell body.
scenes.caption: Picture a plus-end-out track. Its plus end points away from the cell body.
scenes.visual: The arrow placed in a process with its head pointing away from the cell body. Label: plus-end-out.
scenes.narration: Picture a plus-end-out track. Its plus end points away from the cell body.

scenes.tts: On that track, kinesin walks outward. Dynein walks home, toward the cell body.
scenes.visual: Kinesin moves outward; dynein moves back to the cell body.
scenes.narration: On that track, kinesin walks outward. Dynein walks home, toward the cell body.

scenes.tts: On a minus end out track, it is the reverse.
scenes.caption: On a minus-end-out track, it is the reverse.
scenes.visual: The arrow flips. Dynein now moves outward and kinesin moves home. Label: minus-end-out.
scenes.narration: On a minus-end-out track, it is the reverse.

scenes.tts: So which way do the tracks point in a real neuron?
scenes.visual: The neuron map returns, with question marks on its axon and a dendrite.
scenes.narration: So which way do the tracks point in a real neuron?

scenes.tts: In 1988, Peter Baas and colleagues used hook decoration on cultured rat hippocampal neurons.
scenes.visual: On screen: Baas and colleagues, 1988, hook decoration.
scenes.narration: In 1988, Peter Baas and colleagues used hook decoration on cultured rat hippocampal neurons.

scenes.tts: Extra tubulin adds curved sheets to each microtubule's wall. In cross section, the hooks curve one way or the other.
scenes.visual: A cross-section with many small circles, each with a curved hook, some clockwise, some anticlockwise.
scenes.narration: Extra tubulin adds curved sheets to each microtubule's wall. In cross section, the hooks curve one way or the other.

scenes.tts: The curve shows which way that microtubule points.
scenes.visual: Hooks colour-coded by curve direction: plus-end-out or minus-end-out.
scenes.narration: The curve shows which way that microtubule points.

scenes.tts: In the axon, nearly all microtubules point their plus ends away from the cell body.
scenes.visual: Axon cross-section: nearly every hook curves the same way. Nearly all arrows in the gold axon point outward, with one or two pointing back. Label: nearly all.
scenes.narration: In the axon, nearly all microtubules point their plus ends away from the cell body.

scenes.tts: In dendrites the orientation is mixed. A large fraction point each way.
scenes.visual: Dendrite cross-section: hooks curve both ways. Arrows in the green dendrite point both directions.
scenes.narration: In dendrites the orientation is mixed. A large fraction point each way.

scenes.tts: So which motor can carry cargo outward into a dendrite, but hardly ever into the axon?
scenes.visual: A kinesin and a dynein, each with cargo, at the fork. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: So which motor can carry cargo outward into a dendrite, but hardly ever into the axon?

scenes.tts: Dynein. It can carry cargo outward only on minus end out tracks.
scenes.caption: Dynein. It can carry cargo outward only on minus-end-out tracks.
scenes.visual: Dynein carries cargo out into the green dendrite on a minus-end-out track.
scenes.narration: Dynein. It can carry cargo outward only on minus-end-out tracks.

scenes.tts: Vertebrate dendrites have many of those tracks. The axon has almost none.
scenes.visual: In the gold axon, dynein moves almost only toward the cell body.
scenes.narration: Vertebrate dendrites have many of those tracks. The axon has almost none.

scenes.tts: Kinesin can walk outward in both, since both have plus end out tracks.
scenes.caption: Kinesin can walk outward in both, since both have plus-end-out tracks.
scenes.visual: Kinesin moves outward in both the axon and the dendrite.
scenes.narration: Kinesin can walk outward in both, since both have plus-end-out tracks.

scenes.tts: But a kinesin that prefers stable, plus end out microtubules can be steered into the axon.
scenes.caption: But a kinesin that prefers stable, plus-end-out microtubules can be steered into the axon.
scenes.visual: A kinesin carrying gold cargo picks the stable tracks and enters the axon.
scenes.narration: But a kinesin that prefers stable, plus-end-out microtubules can be steered into the axon.

scenes.tts: So the way the tracks point limits which motors can carry cargo outward into a process.
scenes.visual: On screen: the tracks limit the motors.
scenes.narration: So the way the tracks point limits which motors can carry cargo outward into a process.

scenes.tts: That gives the neuron a sorting rule.
scenes.visual: Cargo sorts at the fork: dendritic cargo on dynein to green; axonal cargo on kinesin to gold.
scenes.narration: That gives the neuron a sorting rule.

scenes.tts: The uniform plus end out array may form as the axon forms.
scenes.caption: The uniform plus-end-out array may form as the axon forms.
scenes.visual: Replay of stage 3: as one neurite turns gold, its arrows line up outward. Label: one reading.
scenes.narration: The uniform plus-end-out array may form as the axon forms.

scenes.tts: If so, the tracks may help choose the axon, as well as keep it.
scenes.visual: Two labels on the gold neurite: choose? and keep.
scenes.narration: If so, the tracks may help choose the axon, as well as keep it.

scenes.tts: Flies differ. Their dendrites are mostly minus end out.
scenes.caption: Flies differ. Their dendrites are mostly minus-end-out.
scenes.visual: A fly neuron: dendrite arrows mostly point toward the cell body; axon arrows point out.
scenes.narration: Flies differ. Their dendrites are mostly minus-end-out.

scenes.tts: So the details depend on the animal. But in both, axon and dendrites offer different tracks.
scenes.visual: Vertebrate and fly neurons side by side; different tracks in each branch.
scenes.narration: So the details depend on the animal. But in both, axon and dendrites offer different tracks.

scenes.tts: Different tracks, different motors, different cargo. The tracks may be part of the hold. Next, the gate at the start of the axon.
scenes.visual: Closing card: tracks may help hold the win. Next: The Gate, and the Race Reopened.
scenes.narration: Different tracks, different motors, different cargo. The tracks may be part of the hold. Next, the gate at the start of the axon.
